subject: NRSC
title: Environment and Health
description: Key chemical, physical, and social stressors in the environment, and how these affect the health of people and ecosystems. Hazards in air, water, food, and work environments. Historic, current, and future need for environmental health science, from scientific, personal, and practical perspectives.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who are taking or have taken GEOG 221.

notes: Note: Students enrolled in main campus programs register as GEOG 221; students enrolled in Macdonald campus programs register as NRSC 221. Course is only offered at Macdonald campus.

subject: NRSC
title: Pollution and Bioremediation
description: The environmental contaminants which cause pollution; sources, amounts and transport of pollutants in water, air and soil; waste management.

subject: NRSC
title: Research in Ecology and Development in Africa
description: Development of observation and independent inquiry skills through: 1) participation in short-term project modules in collaboration with existing researchers; 2) participation in interdisciplinary team research on topics selected to allow comparative analysis of field sites; 3) active and systematic observation, documentation, and integration of field experience in ecology and development issues.

corequisites.text: ANTH or GEOG 451 Society & Development in Africa

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking BIOL 451. Open to U2 or later students in the African Field Study Semester (AFSS).

subject: NRSC
title: Water and Health
description: Anticipate, recognize, evaluate, and control water-related hazards such as: biological, chemical, and physical. Considerations for public health and environmental management.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken PARA 515. Open to U3 students and above.
